draft:
hey, this is going to be long because i want to give you the full picture before you start. i'm helping a small dental clinic (three dentists, two receptionists) move off their spreadsheet-based appointment system onto a proper web app. i'm doing it as a favour for my aunt who owns it, so there is no budget and no deadline, but i want to do it properly. i need you to help me write a requirements document i can show to her and to a friend who will review the technical side. everything below matters, please dont summarise it away.

how it works today: the receptionists keep one google sheet per dentist, one tab per month. a row is an appointment with the patient name, phone number, the treatment type, start time and a notes column. double bookings happen about twice a month because two receptionists edit at the same time, and that is the number one reason they want to change. a double booking is when two patients are given the same dentist at the same time, and the new system must make that impossible, not just warn about it. the second problem is that nobody sends reminders, so about 15 percent of patients simply dont show up, which my aunt says costs the clinic around RM 4,000 a month.

users: receptionists can create, move and cancel appointments for any dentist. dentists can only see their own schedule and add clinical notes to an appointment, and they cannot see other dentists' notes. my aunt, the owner, can see everything including a monthly report, but she should not be able to edit clinical notes either, only read them. there is no patient login at all in the first version, patients only get messages. every login must use a username and password with a lockout after 5 wrong attempts, and receptionists share a single front desk computer so the session must time out after 10 minutes of no activity.

appointments: treatment types have different lengths, for example a check-up is 30 minutes, a filling is 45, a root canal is 90, and whitening is 60. the system should pick the length from the treatment type but the receptionist can override it. the clinic is open monday to friday 9am to 6pm and saturday 9am to 1pm, closed on sundays and public holidays, and the lunch break 1pm to 2pm on weekdays is not bookable. buffer: every appointment needs a 10 minute cleaning gap after it before the next one with the same dentist. appointments can be booked at most 6 months ahead. if a dentist is on leave, the system should block their whole day and show the receptionist a list of existing appointments that need to be moved, it should not silently cancel them.

reminders: send an SMS 2 days before and again 2 hours before. the SMS must say the clinic name, the date and time, and a phone number to call to cancel, and nothing about the treatment because that is private health information. if a patient replies CANCEL, the appointment should be marked as cancelled and the slot freed up, and the receptionist should see it flagged. i havent chosen an SMS provider yet, so please compare two or three options and tell me what they roughly cost for about 600 messages a month, and say clearly where you are unsure about prices.

data and privacy: the clinic is in Malaysia so the patient data falls under the PDPA. we need to store only what is needed: name, phone number, date of birth and the notes. no identity card numbers. the data must be backed up every night and the backup must be encrypted, and my aunt must be able to export all of one patient's data and delete it if the patient asks. audit log: every time somebody opens or edits a clinical note, record who and when, and the log cannot be edited by anyone, including my aunt.

the migration: there are about 3 years of old appointments in the sheets, roughly 9,000 rows. i dont want to lose them, but they dont have to be editable, read-only history is fine. phone numbers in the sheets are messy, some start with +60, some with 0, some have dashes or spaces, and a few are clearly typed wrong, so the import must clean them to one format and put the bad ones in a list for the receptionists to fix by hand instead of guessing. the same patient appears with slightly different spellings of their name, and i do not want the importer to merge people automatically, because merging two different patients would be a privacy problem. flag likely duplicates for a human to decide.

tech: i know python and a bit of react, so i would like django with postgres and a simple react or even plain server-rendered front end, hosted on one small cheap server in a malaysian or singapore region so the latency is fine. if you think something else is clearly better for a clinic this size, say so and explain why, but dont switch just because it is fashionable. the front desk computer is old, runs windows 10 and chrome, so the pages must be light and work well on it. the app has to keep working if the internet drops for a few minutes, or at least not lose what the receptionist was typing.

rollout: i want to run the old sheets and the new app side by side for two weeks, with a clear day where we switch over, and a way to go back to the sheets if the first week goes badly. the receptionists are not technical, so there needs to be a one page guide with screenshots and a 30 minute training session. one of them, Mei Ling, has already said she is afraid of change, so the design must be very simple and the main screen must be the day view with big, clear appointment blocks. colour must not be the only way to show a status, because one dentist is colour blind, so use text labels or icons too.

reports: my aunt wants a monthly report ready by the 2nd of each month with appointments per dentist, the no-show rate, the number of cancellations, and income by treatment type. she wants it as a pdf to read and a csv to keep, and she wants to compare it with the previous month. the no-show rate is the main number, because the whole point is to bring the 15 percent down, so it should be the first thing on the page. income is only what the clinic charged for the treatment, the app does not take payments in the first version, and the receptionists type the amount in when the patient pays.

daily operations: two of the dentists like paper, so every morning at 8:30 the system should print that dentist's day schedule, with the appointment times, patient names and treatment types and nothing else. walk-ins are common: each dentist should keep 2 urgent slots per day that stay open until 10am and then open up for normal booking if nobody used them. when somebody cancels, the receptionist should see a waiting list of patients who asked for an earlier time, and be able to offer the slot with one click, but the system must not message the waiting patients on its own.

what i want you to produce: first, a requirements document with sections for users and permissions, appointment rules, reminders, data and privacy, migration, technical choices and rollout. second, a list of open questions i still have to ask my aunt, with the ones that block the design first. third, a rough order of work in small steps, each one something i can finish in a weekend. keep my numbers and names exactly, mark anything you had to assume so i can check it with her, and please do not make the document sound generic. if two of my requirements conflict, tell me instead of picking one quietly.
